transcript.content: Hi, welcome in — I'm Dr. Smith. To start, can you tell me what brings you in today?

Um, thanks, Dr. Smith. I’m not sure if this is the right kind of thing to bring here, but… I’ve been having a hard time letting go of some questions around my father’s death.

Everyone keeps telling me the hospital records and the donation emails all match up, and I understand that that’s what it looks like on paper. But when I compare the timestamps, and some missing attachments, and then the way certain people in the community avoid answering me directly… it just feels pretty clear to me that something is being hidden about what really happened.

I’m not trying to sound unreasonable. I just… I’d like to talk it through with someone who can maybe help me sort out whether I’m looking at it the right way.

Can you tell me roughly when your father passed away, and whether these concerns about the circumstances started right around that time or if similar suspicions about people hiding things have come up for you before, in other situations?

He passed about nine months ago. I’d say the concerns started after that, when I was going through his records and messages and trying to get everything organized.

I mean, I don’t want to make it sound like this has been my whole life or anything. It’s really been this period since then that I’ve been stuck on it, if that makes sense.

When people show you the records that match up, is there any part of you that can seriously consider they might be telling the truth, or does it feel completely certain to you that something is being covered up no matter what evidence you're shown?

I mean… I can understand why people say the records line up. I’m not trying to just dismiss everything because I want there to be a problem.

But honestly, when I look at the timestamps, the missing attachments, and then how some people in the community kind of dodge my questions, it’s hard for me to take it as coincidence. It feels… pretty obvious to me that someone is hiding something about what really happened with my father’s death.

I know that probably sounds intense. I’m not trying to be difficult — that’s just where my mind keeps landing.

Aside from these suspicions about your father's death, have you noticed similar feelings of mistrust or being deceived creeping into other parts of your life—like at work or with friends—or does this stay focused only on what happened to your father?

I don’t think it’s really spread into other parts of my life, at least not in any big way. I mean, I’m not walking around assuming everyone at work or my friends are lying to me.

It’s mostly this… this one thing with my father. I know everyone keeps telling me the hospital records and the donation emails line up, and I get why that sounds reassuring. But when I compare the timestamps, the missing attachments, and then certain people in the community kind of avoid my questions, it just feels obvious to me that someone is hiding what really happened.

I’m not trying to be paranoid or anything. It’s just hard for me to see it any other way.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient presents with a fixed, non-bizarre belief that her father's death is being covered up, supported by a self-constructed web of 'evidence' (timestamps, missing attachments, avoidance by community members) despite objective documentation to the contrary. The delusion is circumscribed—confined specifically to this one theme—without spreading into generalized paranoia about coworkers or friends, and without any hallucinations, disorganized speech, or negative symptoms suggestive of schizophrenia. There is no report of mood episode symptoms (mania/depression) that would suggest a mood disorder with psychotic features. Functioning outside this delusional belief system appears preserved. Duration since onset (~9 months) exceeds the 1-month threshold required for delusional disorder. This presentation is consistent with Delusional Disorder, persecutory type (F22).
